hook.line: Tomás has to call people he has never met, and on the phone you cannot point at anyone. A small set of polite lines gets you to the right person.
hook.en: Could I speak to Andrés, please?

examples.en: Could I speak to Andrés, please?
I wanted to speak to the manager.

examples.es: En este momento no se encuentra.
examples.en: She isn't in at the moment.

rule:
On the phone you ask for a person with *con*: *hablar con Andrés*. Three polite openers:

*¿Podría hablar con...?* Could I speak to...?
*¿Se encuentra...?* Is... there?
*Quería hablar con...* I wanted to speak to...

The answers you will hear:
*¿De parte de quién?* Who's calling?
*Ya se lo paso.* I'll put him on.
*En este momento no se encuentra.* She isn't in right now.

Use *quería* and *podría*, not *quiero* and *puedo*: they are softer.
smallPrint: Teachers call *podría* and *quería* the conditional and imperfect of politeness: both soften a request.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right form and type the whole sentence (Could I speak to Andrés, please?): ¿Podría hablar ___ Andrés, por favor? (con / a)
yourTurn.why: On the phone you speak *con* a person.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Is Dr Ruiz there?
yourTurn.why: *Se encuentra* is the phone way to ask whether someone is there.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I wanted to speak to the manager.
Type in Spanish (as the person answering): Who's calling?
yourTurn.why: This is the set phrase for asking who is calling.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish (you pass the phone to him): I'll put him on now.
yourTurn.why: *Ya se lo paso* is the usual line for putting someone on.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: She isn't in at the moment.
yourTurn.answer: En este momento no se encuentra.
yourTurn.why: *No se encuentra* tells you she is not there.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about Vale: ¿Podría hablar con Andrés, por favor?

pitfalls.why: Almost. On the phone you speak *con* a person, not *a*.
It is understood, but *quería* is much more polite.
When answering, *¿De parte de quién?* is the polite way to ask who is calling.
